entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hélion de Villeneuve was a French-born Grand Master of the Knights of St. John, a military order tasked with protecting Christian pilgrims in the Holy Land.

As Grand Master, he played a crucial role in the defense of the Knights' stronghold on the island of Rhodes, which was besieged by the Ottoman Empire in 1346.

Hélion's leadership during this period showcased the military prowess and strategic thinking of the Knights, who were instrumental in slowing the Ottoman advance.

However, the eventual fall of Rhodes to the Ottomans in 1522 marked a significant turning point in the history of the Knights, who were eventually absorbed into the Knights of Malta.

"The Lord of Rhodes will be saved," Hélion de Villeneuve is quoted as saying in a 1345 letter to the Knights' Hospital in Jerusalem, reflecting the faith and determination of the Knights in the face of overwhelming odds.
